summary: SL-049 turned SL-024's throwaway cloud-filter harness into a tracked, Trait-gated opt-in test. It added tests/CfProvider (a separate-process provider that never answers a callback), a SyncRootRig, a stall Fact and a dehydrated-tree Fact, plus a default-suite guard on opt-in Traits and widened Fitness rules. There was no production code change. The code landed and the default suite is green (332 passed). The two Facts that prove the slice's point, the shipped Scanner and SynchronousIoCancel on a real cldflt folder, have never run in the repo's own build. Design open question 1, whether a sync root may be registered on this PC, was never answered, and validate was accepted from a prior report with no contact.

payload.summary: SL-049 turned SL-024's throwaway cloud-filter harness into a tracked, Trait-gated opt-in test. It added tests/CfProvider (a separate-process provider that never answers a callback), a SyncRootRig, a stall Fact and a dehydrated-tree Fact, plus a default-suite guard on opt-in Traits and widened Fitness rules. There was no production code change. The code landed and the default suite is green (332 passed). The two Facts that prove the slice's point, the shipped Scanner and SynchronousIoCancel on a real cldflt folder, have never run in the repo's own build. Design open question 1, whether a sync root may be registered on this PC, was never answered, and validate was accepted from a prior report with no contact.
payload.estimate_error: Sized medium / medium risk by a person, with 1 designer. The code size was about right: build 1 delivered the design as written, and build 2 fixed only two minor findings. The process cost was badly under-sized: design ran twice, critique twice, build twice, code-review three times and validate six times, with 25 obligations raised. The risk tier was framed as code risk. The real exposure was authorisation. The deliverable's only proof registers a system-level cldflt sync root under the person's %TEMP% and the teardown deletes recursively there. Nobody was present to approve that, and SL-024 validate had already declined the same step. A slice whose acceptance run needs a person's yes should have been tiered and opened with that yes as a precondition.
what_went_wrong: The slice's central claim was never run in the repo's own build. The stall Fact and the tree Fact are compiled and unrun, and the 'teardown shape: PENDING' line has never been produced. Validate finally accepted at HEAD 91dfe9c with contact 'none', taken from validate-4's report. Only the spikes, on scratch copies, ever touched a real sync root.

Design open question 1 (may validate register a real sync root on this PC) was never answered, yet design attempt 2 was accepted 'as composed'. Validate then halted on it at #1, #3, #4 and #5, and #3, #4 and #5 were identical runs at an unchanged HEAD. Each re-ran the build and the 332-test default suite for no new information.

Critique m1 noticed the design had pre-answered that question, but the accepted fix was to reword the key decision. It did not require the answer before build or say the deliverable would be unprovable without it.

Code-review #2 passed with O-024 and O-025 still accepted-pending. Validate #2 then failed and sent the slice back to build. That cost an extra build, an extra code-review and two validate laps. Pending fixes should have gone to build before validate.

Validate could not tell whether question 1 had been answered, because the brief clips the answered-questions list at Q-016. 'No answer on record' was therefore weaker evidence than it was reported to be.

The spike stage downloaded SDK 10.0.401 (about 300 MB) into scratch folders on at least three separate experiments. The build survey refused to run eng/dotnet.ps1 even though Q-003 authorises it. Both left the repo-build seams (ProjectReference to an Exe, muxer launch) open until build.

The design's claim that every run tears down with the provider killed while the request is pending was false on the passing path. The cancel withdraws the request first, and the design had no way to observe which shape ran. Code review had to fix this by adding a second held listing, which makes the stall Fact up to 10 s slower.

New and widened Fitness rules were only checked by Fitness op=check (50 rules hold). rules-parity, the RuleCases runs and harness.py cross-engine agreement were not run at all. The RuleCases.ps1 pin of 28 settled entries was already stale (HEAD had 32) before this slice.

learned.lesson: An opt-in test whose only proof registers a real cldflt sync root needs a person's yes recorded before design is accepted. Do not queue validate for it. SL-024 and SL-049 have now both ended 'not reached' on the same step, and the design's own key decision assumed a yes that question 1 left open. If no standing answer exists at open, either get it then or size the slice as 'ships unproven'. Do not let it go through the gates and stall at validate.
learned.evidence: Open question 1 stayed unanswered through design #2, critique #2, build #2 and code-review #3. Validate halted or failed five times on it. SL-024 validate declined the equivalent step. Only the spike stage ever ran a real sync root.

learned.lesson: When validate halts on a person's unanswered question and HEAD has not moved, re-running validate produces the same report. Route to the question and stop re-running. Also route accepted-pending review findings to build before validate, not after.
learned.evidence: Validate #3, #4 and #5 are identical at 91dfe9c. Code-review #2 passed with O-024 and O-025 pending. Validate #2 then sent the slice back to build, which forced build #2 and code-review #3.

learned.lesson: A validate report of 'no answer on record' does not settle whether a question was answered. The brief truncates the answered-questions list at Q-016. Check the question store directly before treating the question as still open, or before re-asking it.
learned.evidence: Validate #4 lists 'the brief clips it at Q-016, so an answer recorded after that point would not have reached this run'. The list in this reflection also ends at Q-016.

learned.lesson: Opt-in gating in Core.Tests is three coupled pieces: a Trait, a clause in FsaDefaultTestFilter, and an exact-clause check in Unfiltered() (which rejects '|', '(' and ')'). Skip and Explicit are forbidden by CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped. Never bake $(VSTestTestCaseFilter) into anything, because `dotnet test --filter` forwards it as a global property that overrides the csproj value. A new opt-in Trait must be added to FsaDefaultTestFilter and to the OptInTraitTests known-pair pin. A Trait added without the filter clause runs in the default suite and would register a real sync root.
learned.evidence: Critique M1 was confirmed at FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj:9 (Condition on VSTestTestCaseFilter). O-013 and O-018 fixed it. The code-review drift note says OptInTraitTests pins the three known pairs.

learned.lesson: The launch chain of the provider (ProjectReference to the CfProvider Exe, the muxer plus tests runtimeconfig, and eng/dotnet.ps1 forwarding --filter) is now proven without registering anything. Run `--filter FullyQualifiedName~CloudPlaceholderTests.AProviderThatCannotStart`. Do not re-spike it. CloudRigTests (26 tests) and OptInTraitTests (10) run in the default suite. Only the two Facts that register a root are unrun.
learned.evidence: Validate #4 ran both AProviderThatCannotStart Facts: 'ERR CfRegisterSyncRoot hr=0x80070002', exit 2 in 74 ms, and a kill at 2 s with no READY. Teardown took 1-4 ms and left no fsa-cf-* folder. The design listed these seams as unmeasured items (a)-(c).

learned.lesson: Cloud-folder scanner behaviour that any future scanner or UI slice must design around: a stalled FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS never times out by itself (cldflt re-issues at 60.48 s) and the guard has no stall deadline, so only Stop ends the scan. After Stop the stalled folder is an empty Folder in a Cancelled result and is not in ScanResult.Unreadable. The stall Fact pins this as a characterization, so a scanner change to report it will fail that test on purpose and must update it.
learned.evidence: Spike stalled-fetch-placeholders-shipped-scanner-cancels (conditional, constraints 1 and 2). Cancel freed the scan in 32 ms. With no cancel it was still blocked at 75 s.

learned.lesson: Treat the first real `--filter Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT` run as a spike, not a regression check. The tree scenario (population-disabled dirs, a never-answering provider, a provider-made hardlink) was run by no spike, and the hardlink assertions are marked UNMEASURED. HoldListing's second listing may raise no fresh FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS, so 'teardown shape: PENDING' may never appear. The class remarks state the pending shape as fact while the code only logs it. A first failure may be a setup defect or a counting-rule question for the person, not a scanner bug.
learned.evidence: Code-review #3 drift notes. Validate #4 'not reached' list. Design m6 and coherence-check item (d). Build #2 left the stall Fact 'compiled but never run'.

learned.lesson: A green Fitness op=check is one engine only. Validate has no TAAD engine interpreter, so rules-parity, RuleCases C-001..C-014 and harness.py cross-engine agreement have not run on this slice's widened patterns or the new InteropLivesOnlyInNative exemptions. RuleCases.ps1's pin of 28 settled entries was stale before this slice. A slice that edits fitness.yaml should say who runs the parity check.
learned.evidence: Validate #4 not-run list. The code-review drift note says the '28 settled' pin was stale (HEAD had 32). Build-slice attempt 1 follow-ups.

learned.lesson: For a single-designer medium slice that builds new test infrastructure with real OS side effects, the critique is where the rework was cheapest and it earned its cost. Its three majors (the MSBuild global-property override, the hardlink or FETCH_DATA hang path, and the confinement-rule bypasses) all survived into the accepted design. Skipping critique-review by sizing cost nothing visible. Budget the person-facing waits (unanswered design questions, findings waiting on a decision) as the dominant cost, not build time.
learned.evidence: Critique #1 halted with 11 findings and design #1 halted on 2 questions. Both build attempts were small (build #2 changed two test files). Design and critique waits plus the validate loop accounted for most of the 6 validate, 3 code-review and 2 design runs.

missed.what: The design's key decision said validate 'runs --filter Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT once on this PC' while open question 1 (may a sync root be registered) was unanswered. Critique m1 was filed as a minor rewording. Nobody asked what validate reports if the answer is no. The critique did not require the answer before build, although SL-024 validate had already declined the same step.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice: halted or failed at #1, #2, #3, #4 and #5 at the same unanswered question. It was accepted only via a none-contact pass at #6.

missed.what: The design and O-006 claimed every run takes the kill-while-FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS-pending teardown that spike 4 measured. On the passing path, cts.Cancel() frees the listing and the provider's CANCEL_FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS can withdraw the request before Dispose kills the provider. The design gave no way to observe which shape ran. The critique did not ask what state the request is in at the kill.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (m1, then O-024); fixed in build #2 with a held second listing and a 'teardown shape:' line.

missed.what: The sweep runs a real CfUnregisterSyncRoot and a recursive Directory.Delete on names under %TEMP%. The critique filed sweep findings (m4 on pid liveness, m5 on the predicate) but never asked about a junction or symlink carrying a dead root's name. This project already has Q-001 requiring junction and symlink coverage. The builder's LinkTarget guard was the only protection and no test fed it.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (m2, then O-025); a mutation run that removed the guard made the new test fail.

missed.what: The design put new P/Invoke code in CloudPlaceholderTests.cs and tests/CfProvider/Program.cs. Its coherence check only considered rule-engine regex syntax (alternation, \b, literals). It never checked the change against the existing InteropLivesOnlyInNative rule. The build had to add exemptions to that rule, and nothing has yet checked them across both engines. This is inferred from validate's mention of 'new InteropLivesOnlyInNative exemptions', not from a recorded finding.
missed.caught_by: build-slice (the exemptions were added there); cross-engine agreement was still not-run at validate.

unknowns: Was design open question 1 ever answered? Validate could not tell, because the brief clips the answered list at Q-016. If it was answered yes, the opt-in run was owed and skipped. If never answered, it still gates the slice's real proof.

Does a second listing of 'stall' after a cancelled first one raise a fresh this-process FETCH_PLACEHOLDERS on a real sync root? If it does not, the 'teardown shape: PENDING' line is never produced and C-006 needs another way in.
Does the tree scenario (population-disabled directories, a never-answering provider, a provider-made hardlink) set up cleanly? Does the hardlink pair charge once? No spike ran this scenario.

Does killing the provider free a scan blocked on a pending FETCH_DATA, and does CancelSynchronousIo do so? The shipped scanner never raises FETCH_DATA, so only a provider that answers, or a hydrating regression, can produce it.
Do the widened SL-049 Fitness patterns and the InteropLivesOnlyInNative exemptions agree between rules-parity.ps1 and harness.py?

candidates.title: Run `--filter Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT` three times on this PC and record the stall Fact's 'teardown shape:' lines
candidates.why: The slice was accepted without its central claim running. This is the first real evidence for the shipped Scanner and SynchronousIoCancel on a real cf-filter folder, for C-006 and for the tree Fact's hardlink assertions. It depends on design open question 1, which is already on the list. Afterwards, correct the class remarks (CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:22-26) to state whichever shape was actually observed.

candidates.title: Repair the tests/rules pin and run the cross-engine rules checks for SL-049's Fitness changes
candidates.why: The RuleCases.ps1 pin of 28 settled entries was stale before this slice (HEAD had 32). rules-parity.ps1, RuleCases C-001..C-014 and harness.py agreement were not run on the widened src/** and Core.Tests patterns or the InteropLivesOnlyInNative exemptions. They need the TAAD engine interpreter, which validate lacks.

candidates.title: Add a provider mode that answers callbacks late, with an error, or with real data transfer
candidates.why: The provider never answers, so a late or error reply, a partial on-disk size, and a kill freeing a pending FETCH_DATA were measured by no stage. The design refused a partial-hydration arm because spike 2's run1 setup defect came from a data-answering provider. This is the follow-up once the first real run is green.

candidates.title: Decide how the app tells the user a scan is stalled on an unresponsive cloud folder
candidates.why: The spike showed the guard has no stall deadline and cldflt only re-issues the callback at 60.48 s, so the scan hangs until Stop. After Stop the folder appears as an empty Folder and not in Unreadable. Any fix to either would change the stall Fact's characterization assertion, so it belongs in a scanner or UI slice, not in this test.
